en: What do I do then?
Aw geez, sir. Get to know them personally and then negotiate with them on the down-low! Just ask them if they wanna come visit Tokyo.
That sounds like it'll take forever. I mean, I can maybe work on one girl like that, but I can't be everywhere at once. I'd need help.
I suppose so, sir.
But the idea does have some merit, I'll admit. If I know someone who's hitting up any of those other cities, I'll let you know.
I knew I could count on you, sir! In the meantime, I'll do what I can with the club on my end.
That's the spirit. I knew I hired you as manager for a reason.
Hehehe. Guess you saw my limitless potential, sir!
Oh, speaking of which, keep working on this diamond in the rough you found, too, yeah?
Of course! You can count on me!
Well? You want the lozenge?
You said all the money I have, right?
Yep. If you're wantin' to make that girl's dreams come true, it ain't gonna come cheap.
The heck ya want?
There's something I'm looking for, and I thought someone here at the park might be able to help me out.
What in the world are ya lookin' for?
Sell me some medicine.
I don't know nothin' about that. Go on, get outta here.
(Looks like telling him to give me medicine was a no-go. I need to change up my approach.)
(He's acting like he's hiding something. He won't just hand over what I want. Maybe there's some clue I can find.)
Tsk. The heck is yer problem?
Sell me a dream.
What kinda dream?
There's a girl who wants to be a newscaster. She worked day and night to fix her Kansai accent, and now her voice is shot right before the test.
Well, now. Sounds rough.
I heard there's some legendary lozenge that could help her. Do you have any?
I do indeed.
Really? Please, you have to give it to me.
You got cash on ya?
Everything ya got on ya.
Hey, ya want the lozenge, don't ya? Ya wanna make this girl's dream come true?
No way. I won't pay that much.
You're the one who said this is her dream. If ya don't have high enough hopes for her, then givin' her the medicine won't mean a darn thing.
It's not about money. Dreams aren't only for the people that can afford them. They're made of the hopes and desires of everyone else around them.
Something that important can't possibly be bought with money.
Hmph. I see.
Ya don't get it at all, do ya?
Ain't no room for pretty sentiments like that in the broadcast industry. Money talks in show biz. Money's what makes people tick.
If ya really have high hopes for that girl, show it with money. If ya can't do that, ya might as well give up.
All right. I'll give you all the money I have.
Ya serious? Why are ya stickin' yer neck out like that? This girl got that much talent?
I want to see her achieve her dreams. That's all there is to it. Whether she's got the talent for it or not, I don't know.
So her dreams are worth yer investment?
No, I don't think so. You can't assign a monetary value to a dream.
A million or ten billion yen, no matter how much money you throw at your dreams, you'll never reach them. Because dreams have limitless value.
If this makes her dreams come true, then I don't care if you take all my money. It's that simple.
Heh. Ain't met a guy like you in a long time.
I've been runnin' this scam job, hopin' to meet a man like you.
Whether it's a sore throat or a scandal...
When performers wind up in trouble, they find out how much money their talent agency is willin' to spend on 'em.
To the agency, the talent is their meal ticket. If it ain't worth their investment, they'll drop her. They don't care if the talent succeeds.
Well, that's the cruel business world for you.
Yeah, but sometimes someone's worth the investment, regardless of the bottom line. There's just somethin' about 'em.
Yer expectations for this girl come from ya seein' some kinda unique spark in her, I bet.
I guess that's one way to put it.
Here's the legendary lozenge. Take it.
If she sucks on this and gets a bit a' rest, her voice'll be right as rain.
Really? Thank you so much. You're a lifesaver. Here, let me get you your money.
Forget the money.
I wanted to see how far ya were willin' to go for this dream. Now that I know, it's all good.
You... Thank you so much.
Don't thank me. I'll just watch with ya to see if this dream comes true. Now go on, hurry up and get that medicine to her.
(I should shoot Honoka-chan an email.)
Hey, I got you some medicine. I'm sure it will make you better.
Aaah. Aaah...
It really worked! My voice is back!
Thank goodness. But you'd better not talk yet. You need to rest up for a while, then I'm sure you'll be back to normal.
Hm? You're trying to say something. What is it?
"Since just resting is boring, I'd like you to stay here with me while I'm sucking on this lozenge, Akiyama-san."
"And since I want to keep practicing my Tokyo accent, I'd like you to talk to me the entire time."
What's this now?
Not bad, right? You can hang out and help my vocal practice!
Guess I'd better. You just leave it to Nurse Akiyama.
Shion-chan!
You're not hurt or anything?
No, I'm fine.
So where's this stalker of yours?
I think... Behind that street light over there.
That guy over there?
Hey, stop!
All right, buddy, start talking. Who are you?
I'm... I'm with Kinei Detective Agency.
You're a detective!? So you're not a stalker. Are you protecting her?
Wait. Shion-chan never said anything about hiring a detective.
No, I've been asked to conduct a background check on the young lady. I can only assume she mistook me for a stalker.
A background check? For who?
I'm not at liberty to say. It's my policy as an investigator to maintain my clients' privacy.
Hm. You could be anyone for all I know. I'm betting I can still turn you over to the police. Taking photos of people without them knowing is still a crime.
Then I'll simply claim that photography is a hobby of mine. I simply take pictures of what I see. Since when is that against the law?
Ha! So that's how it's gonna be, huh?
All right, then instead of the cops, how about I turn you over to the Nagoya Family?
The... The Nagoya Family!?
Yeah. I'm guessing you've heard of them?
Listen, man! I'll talk! I'll talk!
(Heh. Being on the other side of a threat like this sure is bizarre.)
The client who hired me to investigate Shion-san is an executive at one of the leading companies in Nagoya.
What!? Then that means...
Yes. Someone has asked for her hand in marriage.
So why the investigation?
It's not uncommon for influential families to conduct a background check on a potential spouse. It would be problematic if they had associations with an undesirable crowd.
An undesirable crowd? Shion-chan might not be at your client's level, but she's from a pretty wealthy family too. She can't possibly be trouble.
Actually, my investigation has turned up some alarming facts.
Alarming facts?
As it turns out, Shion-san owes a considerable amount of money.
Well, technically her parents do. They've sold off their mansion and are now living in an apartment that costs 70,000 yen per month.
She hasn't said a word about any of this.
Nagoya women are a prideful sort. She wouldn't want to tarnish her reputation.
It can't be...
Ah! Shion-chan!
Did you hear all that?
Investigator-san, is it true that you were hired to perform a background check on me?
Yes, miss. And unfortunately, at this point, I'm afraid my client is likely to rescind his marriage proposal.
Pedigree is everything in Nagoya. Despite your family's good name and long history, he cannot marry into a legacy that has fallen from grace.
Have you come to laugh at me? At the lying girl who pretended to be rich when she was poor all along?
Of course not. How can you even think that of me, Shion-chan?
I wouldn't want to be judged by how much money I don't have. I'm not going to do that to anyone else either.
So can you tell me what's going on? Is it true you're in debt?
It is...
But how?
My father's business failed, and we were left with nothing but debt. He worked so hard to try to turn things around, but the fatigue and stress was just too much.
Your father worked himself to death.
Didn't you think it was strange, Shinada-san? A proper Nagoya woman has no business being a hostess.
None of my other friends rejoice in receiving gifts from clients, or have to work so hard sending out emails to maintain good business.
Ever since my father passed away, my mother has become so weak. I'm the only one who can possibly repay our debts.
And that's why you got a job as a hostess.
I thought if I worked hard enough, I could pay off those debts, and we could live our happy life from before.
When that client asked me to marry him, I was hesitant at first. But I decided to accept, in order to save my family.
I guess that's out now too, huh?
This is all because we don't have money anymore. When it comes down to it, our family's lineage and good name are worth nothing.
That's not true, Shion-chan.
Even if you don't have money, it's being together that makes you a happy family.
So what if you're poor, or if you pretend to have more than you do? The important thing is whether or not you're proud of the life you're living.
What do you want more than anything, Shion-chan? To live a life of luxury?
Or is it to have your family back to the way it was, when all three of you were happy?
I hadn't thought about it like that. As long as my family was happy again, I wouldn't care if we didn't have any money.
That's the spirit!
I... I will decline the marriage proposal.
I think I've had quite enough of men who care only about my family's background!
Hahaha! There's the Shion-chan I know!
Instead, I found a man who was kind enough to tell me he doesn't care if I'm poor.
I can't ask for anything more than to spend time with someone who accepts me for who I am.
Do you mean...?
Shinada-san, would you like to be my boyfriend?
Really? Me!? You bet I would!
Yes! And in exchange, I want to know everything there is to know about you!
Your home is far nicer than I expected, Shinada-san!  I imagined you were a man of far more modest means.
Hey, I know how to work hard! I always make sure my place is guest-ready.
Then maybe we can work together to pay off my family's debts.
Right. How much do you owe, anyway?
So, it's actually...
Whoooa! That much!?
My father's business was liable for quite a lot. Personal debts are nothing compared to what a company can accrue.
I can see something like that would lead to bankruptcy.
Oh, but this will be such fun, Shinada-san! Just you, me, and my mother! We will surely be quite happy together!
Ahaha... Ha... Yeah...
I'm so lucky to have you by my side, Shinada-san!
Hehe. Thank you, Kiryu-san.
But I got one more piece a' advice to ask ya.
I find myself always wanting to be around ya. What should I do?
I haven't a clue. Whatever you like, I suppose.
Hahaha! Then guess that's what I'll do!
I sure love you, Kiryu-san!
You really do have some pretty big dreams, Saejima-san! I have to say, I'm rather moved!
Looks like they never got back to ya.
You'll have other chances, I'm sure of it. Chin up, and keep goin'.
Well, about that...
They actually said they wouldn't be giving me their decision until a bit later on.
What!? Ya said it'd be real soon!
Yeah, but if I'd told you that, then you wouldn't have stayed here with me!
So you tricked me!?
Come on, don't be like that! I really am very grateful to you.
Hmph. Just lemme know when ya hear back.
Will do! You're the best, Saejima-san!
I owe ya big time, Akiyama-san.
You seem much better now. Guess that really was some legendary lozenge. Your voice is back to normal.
Hehe. It was surprisingly super sweet! Now I kinda want another one.
Hey now, that was a one time deal. I really am quite a busy guy.
Aww, why ya gotta be a wet blanket?
Hey, there's not much time before the test. You need to hurry and get ready.
Yeah! Akiyama-san, I looove ya! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Hey, Kiryu-san?
How come you didn't want to sleep with me?
I really wouldn't have minded, Kiryu-san. Is it because you think I'm a mess?
No, of course not.
Then why?
Hinata, I didn't do what I did just to sleep with you.
I did it because I wanted to win your heart.
You mean...!?
Hinata, men are despicable creatures, who will use money or force to get a woman's body if they are able.
